crime_highlights: He identified himself as a police officer and told Mr. Morris to stop. Mr. Morris kept running.
In the jacket he found a loaded .38 calibre Smith & Wesson handgun
rationale_highlights: The evidence does, however, offer an explanation, rooted in the social context evidence, that explains why Mr. Morris made such a bad and dangerous choice

That explanation points to circumstances, many of which were not only beyond Mr. Morris’s control, but were in fact imposed on him as a consequence of systemic and overt anti-Black racism in various social institutions
There are mitigating factors in this case favouring a sentence at the low end of the range
The moral blameworthiness of Mr. Morris’s conduct is mitigated by his mental and physical health issues, as well as his educational and economic disadvantages
All of those factors are influenced by the systemic anti-Black racism Mr. Morris has experienced
note: Appeal court's own conclusion at para 179; crime facts mostly flight and gun.

crime_highlights: He walked over to a teller, produced an eight-inch knife, and, while brandishing the weapon at the teller, demanded money
The appellant made these threats in the presence of other patrons, including a mother and her two young children
rationale_highlights: The sentencing judge specifically considered the appellant’s Indigenous status
He referenced his judicial duty to give effect to the remedial purpose of s. 718.2(e) of the Criminal Code and to respond to the over-incarceration of Indigenous offenders
It is this very analysis which led the sentencing judge to consider a sentence in the low reformatory range, and to impose a sentence of six months’ incarceration
even accepting the reduced moral responsibility of this offender
I see no error in this analysis that would warrant interference by this court
note: Appeal court endorses trial Gladue analysis; offender's background never described.

crime_highlights: The appellant further admitted that he was aware that ammunition for the sawed off rifle was in his jacket hanging in the same closet
rationale_highlights: The trial judge’s reasons for sentence reveal a careful consideration of the appellant’s personal circumstances and the extensive social context evidence placed before the trial judge
there was much to be said in mitigation of the appellant’s personal blameworthiness and in favour of his rehabilitative potential
Circumstances beyond his control, some of which no doubt reflect systemic racism, diminish his moral culpability
On the record before the trial judge, he was a candidate for a conditional sentence
Given the circumstances of this offender, a conditional sentence on the firearms charge of two years less a day, to be followed by probation for two years, is a fit sentence
note: Short appeal reasons; systemic racism mitigation stated briefly at para 16.
